facts.text: Founding by Hispanic settlers 1867-1872, part of four villages, irrigation agriculture, livestock grazing, communal faith structures.
The community grew from land grants like Rancho de Río Puerco after 1848 Treaty, encouraging Hispanic colonization and irrigation-based farming.
San Luis sits at 6,555 feet, where nighttime temperatures can be 20-30°F cooler than daytime, creating a notable diurnal range.
Mid-20th century uranium mining boom brought prospectors and workers, with over 100 abandoned mines in the county.
The town’s culture is clannish; families’ acceptance determines community inclusion, reflecting its self-sufficient ranching roots.
San Luis lies near the Rio Puerco River, a tributary of the Rio Grande, and close to Cibola National Forest’s ponderosa pine and volcanic badlands.
